clips.send: A friend who works twice as hard as everyone else and still isn't getting ahead - not to guilt them, to show them the gap was never effort; unease, then relief.
clips.caption:
Put a rich brain on a monitor and a poor brain on another, and you won't see motivation. You'll see wavelength.

Kevin says the richest people he knows live in theta and gamma most of the day - the states monks reach after years of practice. Most people live almost entirely in beta, built for worry, not creation.

The part that stings: the hippocampus runs smaller in people who stay broke, and the pineal gland calcifies - not an accident, something done to you.

Comment RISE and I'll send you the exercise that reverses it.

clips.send: Someone who swears they don't have time to read, because this says the habit matters more than the book, and that not reading was never really their own idea; unease, mild anger.
clips.caption:
Keeping a population illiterate was never only about blocking information. Kevin names the reason nobody says out loud: it kept a part of the brain from ever getting stimulated.

He says the content barely matters. A trashy paperback lowers the stress hormone and pulls the brain into the same state as any 'important' book - the state people describe when a goal stops stalling and starts moving.

The book was never the point. The habit was.

Comment RISE and I'll send you the state it puts your brain in.
